sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Developer Infrastructure, Database and API Monitoring Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force 31 October 2012 (includes investment chapter)
Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 April 2013
Panama-Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement, in force 2002
Panama-Spain Double Taxation Agreement, in force 2013
Panama-United Kingdom Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA), in force 2011

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law 41 of 2000 and Law 61 of 24 October 2016; Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT regime); Law 52 of 1 August 2016 (creation of Unidad de Análisis Financiero and beneficial ownership powers); Law 70 of 23 October 2019 and Executive Decree 425 of 29 September 2020 (Final Beneficiaries Registry administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos); Executive Decree 363 of 13 November 2013 (regulation of Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional) executed under Articles 11-13 of Law 25 of 1995
Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) adopting governance, financial and beneficiary provisions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder and Notary Public of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing resident agent and executing agents
Certified true copies of passports or national identity documents of founder, foundation council members, protector and beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent state authority of each individual's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Non-Registration of Name (Certificado de No Inscripción)
Certificate of Legal Existence and Good Standing of corporate founder (if the founder is a legal entity)
Legal opinion on foundation validity and non-taxable foreign-source status

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of founder, foundation council members, protector, final beneficiaries and their immediate family and close associates against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK sanctions lists, international PEP databases (e.g., World-Check, LexisNexis) and Panama's UAF PEP register. Enhanced due diligence is required under Article 13 of Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree 363 of 2013 where any subject is identified as a Politically Exposed Person or is linked to a high-risk jurisdiction or unusual donation (apport). Screening results must be documented in the resident agent's internal AML file, retained for five years, and refreshed annually. Given the business scope (ISIC 6201, DevOps/API cloud infrastructure, payment rails via Stripe Billing and Mercury ACH), the foundation is classified as Low_Risk_Standard and no statutory license is triggered.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Online Services Platform for Name Reservation and Certificado de No Inscripción, https://www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be expressed in any modern alphabet language, but the Foundation Charter must be recorded in Spanish; if the chosen name is in a foreign language, a sworn Spanish transliteration or translation must be endorsed in the charter. Under Law 25 of 1995, the name must be distinctive and must not cause confusion with any existing registered foundation or company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical, visually or phonetically similar to an already registered foundation, corporation or trademark
Words implying national or governmental patronage ('República', 'Ministerio', 'Gobierno', 'Nacional', 'Estado')
Regulated financial tokens ('Banco', 'Financiera', 'Seguros', 'Reaseguros', 'Fondo de Inversión', 'Trust') unless sectorial authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos is produced
Names misleading as to the foundation purpose or contrary to public order and morals
Corporate suffixes such as 'S.A.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.' or 'Corp.' which are inapplicable to Private Interest Foundations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the corresponding registry tariff. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' and, if necessary, a 'Recurso de Apelación' before the Dirección General del Registro Público within five working days of notification, in accordance with Panama's Administrative Procedures Law 38 of 2000; alternatively, a corrected name may be resubmitted, retaining priority if filed within the original reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute: Article 15 of Law 25 of 1995 requires every foundation to maintain a resident agent (agente residente) who is a licensed attorney or licensed law firm with a physical Panamanian office where the registered office is located. Virtual mail-forwarding or remote communication services may complement, but cannot replace, the statutory resident-agent address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard-risk DevOps cloud infrastructure foundation (estimated below 5% annual probability of unannounced inspection in the first year). The primary inspection target of the UAF and Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions supervision is the resident agent and its AML/UBO file; the probability rises meaningfully if the foundation engages in unregistered trust-like activities, receives third-party payments outside the declared SaaS/API monitoring scope, or interacts with high-risk jurisdictions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and certificate of non-registration (Certificado de No Inscripción)
Certified Spanish translation and transliteration endorsement of foreign-language foundation name and documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator or licensing Panamanian counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública) and Foundation Regulations
Public Registry inscription and filing fees (ficha) for the foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on foundation endowment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent engagement and registered office service (first year)
Legal due diligence, drafting of foundation charter, regulations and corporate records
Apostille processing for the notarization bundle originating abroad or in Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Ministry of Foreign Affairs or origin-country competent authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding: UBO file compilation, PEP and OFAC/UN sanctions screening reports
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Resident agent or outsourced compliance provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion on foundation validity, non-taxable foreign-source income status and low-risk classification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, particularly Arts. 1, 3, 6, 12, and 22; Law No. 254 of 2021 establishing the Beneficial Ownership Registry (RUB); provisions of the Public Registry of Panama for registration of private interest foundations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section (Fundaciones de Interés Privado / Private Interest Foundations Unit)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) executed as a public deed (Escritura Pública) before a Panamanian Notary Public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum foundation patrimony of USD 10,000 (or equivalent in assets or any currency); no statutory paid-up capital deposit, no escrow account obligation at formation, and no proof of contribution is filed with the Public Registry. The Foundation Council must maintain the foundation patrimony separately from the founder's personal assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDER AND FIRST FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF PA_PIF. RESOLVED: (1) The initial patrimony is USD 10,000, contributed by the Founder and recorded in the Foundation Deed; (2) the registered office is at the Panamanian registered agent's address, which shall receive all statutory notices; (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed President and Secretary-Treasurer of the Foundation Council, each with authority to act and sign; (4) any one officer may open bank accounts, execute documents, and retain counsel; any two officers may bind the Foundation on ordinary matters; (5) this resolution is effective immediately until amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section (Online and in-person name search window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name-search request using three proposed foundation names in Spanish. The Registry verifies that the preferred name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporation, foundation, or registered trademark. The availability result is used in the Foundation Charter before notarization.
required_dossiers: Name-search application form
Three proposed foundation names
Copy of passport or corporate identification of the applicant or the Panamanian registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, submit an administrative reconsideration to the Public Registry or select one of the alternate proposed names; no additional statutory fee is charged for a secondary name-search request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notaría Pública) selected by the Founder or registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish including the foundation name, duration, purposes, registered office address, initial patrimony, Foundation Council members, Protector provisions (if any), amendment rules, and termination rules. The Founder or attorney-in-fact appears before the notary, declares intent to create the private interest foundation, and executes the public deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or valid identification of the Founder
Power of attorney if signed by a representative
Notarized draft Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación)
Name availability result from the Public Registry
Registered agent acceptance letter with local address
Letter of acceptance from each Foundation Council member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Notary will correct any formal defect and re-execute the deed; if the Registry later refuses content, a corrective deed can be prepared. Notarial fees may increase only if a full re-draft is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section / Private Interest Foundations Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified first notarial copy (copia auténtica) of the Foundation Charter, the completion of the registry's standard application form, and proof of payment of the statutory registration fee. The Registry examines the deed for compliance with Law 25 of 1995, assigns the foundation's mercantile folio number, and issues a certificate of inscription.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the Foundation Charter
Notarial payment receipt
Proof of payment of the USD 250 inscription fee to the Public Registry
Formal registration request letter signed by the Panamanian attorney or registered agent
List of registered office address and Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a preventive note (nota defectuosa) is issued, counsel has 30 calendar days to cure the noted defect and file a corrective brief; substantive omissions may require re-execution of the Foundation Charter before the Notary and a new inscription filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Endorsement and Beneficial Ownership Registry (RUB) Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — RUB portal; supervised by the Panamanian Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent formally accepts the resident-agency engagement for the PIF. After inscription, the agent submits the Beneficial Ownership Registry (RUB) declaration to the DGI within the statutory deadline, including the ultimate beneficial owner's identity, nationality, date of birth, and nature and approximate percentage of interest. The DGI record is kept confidential and is not public.
required_dossiers: Registered agent engagement letter
Registered Foundation Charter and certificate of inscription
RUB declaration form (data of the ultimate beneficial owner and all intermediate entities, if any)
Copy of passport and proof of tax identification of the UBO
Foundation Council member identification, if relevant to control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI issues a requirement or rejects the RUB filing, correct and resubmit through the registered agent's RUB online account within 10 working days; late filings may incur statutory fines but are curable by prompt voluntary filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating Notice (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGI-MEF for RUC registration; Municipality of Panama or the applicable municipal authority for the Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the foundation will earn Panamanian-source income or open a physical office in Panama, apply for an RUC and file the municipal Aviso de Operación. For a pure remote DevOps cloud infrastructure business without a Panama office, no industrial or municipal operating license is required; the foundation may remain registered solely under the Public Registry and the RUB, subject to territorial-source tax treatment.
required_dossiers: Registered Foundation Charter and inscription certificate
RUC registration form if Panamanian-source income is expected
Municipal Aviso de Operación application and fee if a local physical office is opened
Foundation Council resolution designating the officer for tax filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal or DGI rejections are cured by correcting the form, affixing the missing signature, or paying the applicable municipal fee; late Aviso de Operación filings are accepted by the municipality with a late-payment or penalty clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (Software Publishing / DevOps tools / cloud database and API monitoring) is a service classification and does not require an industrial or manufacturing license in Panama. If a physical office is opened, the relevant authority is the municipality issuing the Aviso de Operación.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) — required only for a physical office or local payroll; no specialized operational license exists for cloud database, API, or developer-infrastructure services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — cloud-software service is not listed among Panama's mandatory environmental impact assessment categories; no EIA report, registration, or environmental licence applies to this scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A — the business generates no wastewater, VOC emissions, combustion gases, or hazardous solid waste. If any physical servers are housed, they must be hosted by third-party data centers that hold their own environmental authorizations and comply with Panama's e-waste and energy-efficiency norms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a pure remote DevOps infrastructure service with no brick-and-mortar plant. If a Panama administrative office is later opened, the company must obtain the municipal occupancy permit (permiso de ocupación), a fire-safety inspection certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, and general occupational health clearance under Panama's workplace safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; e-administration portal 'SAT en Línea' at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (e-invoicing platform: Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá / SFEP); customs clearance administered separately through the Panamanian customs administration and its SIGA/VUCEA single-window systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP for a foreign-owned PA_PIF: (1) Execute and inscribe the foundation charter at the Registro Público de Panamá under Ley 25 de 1995, appointing a resident agent; the registered PIF acquires separate legal personality. (2) File the beneficial-ownership declaration (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) through the resident agent. (3) Obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) with the DGI, filing the foundation certificate, Public Registry inscription, by-laws and identity of the legal representative; non-resident founders are permitted and no local share capital deposit is required beyond the statutory minimum. (4) File the national Aviso de Operación (DGI/MICI) only when Panamanian commercial activity is carried out; municipal patent applies to physical premises only. (5) Register as ITBMS taxpayer (general regime) and obtain SFEP e-invoicing credentials to issue zero-rated export invoices. (6) Non-resident digital suppliers may alternatively use the simplified ITBMS registration of Executive Decree 420 of 2017 with a Panamanian fiscal representative. Standard handling: 3-10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope. The PIF is a separate taxable person under Código Fiscal Articles 693-694 and 699, taxed only on Panama-source income; foreign-source dividends, interest, royalties, capital gains and distributions to non-resident beneficiaries fall outside the Panamanian income tax net. ITBMS applies only to supplies used, consumed or exploited in Panama. The PIF is not treated as a tax-transparent pass-through entity for Panamanian purposes, but its non-Panama activities generate no entity-level tax; no Tax-Exempt-Zone status applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no OECD-style check-the-box election. Statutory and administrative elections available to the PA_PIF: (i) voluntary registration as an ITBMS taxpayer to claim input credits and lawfully issue 0% export invoices; (ii) election of the Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes where annual gross receipts do not exceed B/.36,000; (iii) simplified ITBMS registration for non-resident digital service suppliers under Executive Decree 420 of 2017, including the appointment of a fiscal representative; (iv) by-law elections under Ley 25 de 1995 (reserved powers, irrevocable distributions to foreign beneficiaries) which are neutral for Panamanian tax because of territoriality; (v) no hybrid-mismatch or CFC election exists—foreign-only structures may be reorganized without Panamanian tax recognition. Fiscal domicile must be maintained through a resident attorney/agent.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT-equivalent tax on transfers of movable goods and services (Código Fiscal Articles 1057 et seq.).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General domestic regime: no statutory minimum—registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply made or rendered in Panama. Small-taxpayer special regime (Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes): annual gross receipts up to B/.36,000 (US$36,000). Non-resident digital-service suppliers under Executive Decree 420 of 2017: no de minimis threshold—simplified ITBMS registration is mandatory from the first supply to Panamanian recipients, generally collected by withholding of local payment intermediaries. An export-oriented PIF should register voluntarily to issue 0% export invoices and preserve ITBMS credit positions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá / SFEP) phased in since 2020 and compulsory for all taxpayers as of fiscal year 2023 (DGI Resolution 201-6024 of 2020, as amended). Model: online issuance with near-real-time transmission to and validation by the DGI; each invoice is sealed with a DGI authorization token/folio and QR code before delivery to the customer; contingency/offline invoices must be transmitted immediately upon reconnection. Certified billing platforms and ERPs integrate via DGI-approved APIs (SOAP/REST web services). E-credit notes and e-debit notes are synchronized with the same clearance mechanism; export invoices must include the statutory zero-rating legend and supporting export/customs reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated when title passes to a non-resident and the goods are physically exported outside Panama under an accepted export declaration to the customs authority. Services (including DevOps SaaS, database and API-monitoring cloud services, ISIC 6201): zero-rated where the recipient of the service is non-resident and the service is actually used or exploited entirely outside Panama, with the contractual and economic place of benefit abroad. B2B cloud sales to foreign customers qualify provided no Panamanian-resident customer, local establishment or Panama-based use occurs; payment received from abroad (Stripe Billing settlement, Mercury ACH) corroborates the offshore nexus, and the PIF must issue the electronic invoice with the legend 'Exportación de Servicios — 0% ITBMS'.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: E-invoice in SFEP format carrying the DGI validation token and zero-rating/export legend
Panamanian export customs declaration (SIGA/VUCEA) for goods, or DGI-accepted service-export affidavit
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or carrier certificate evidencing physical departure
Export service contract identifying the non-resident recipient, offshore use and place of benefit
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT/MT103, Stripe settlement reports, Mercury ACH account statements
Foreign recipient's tax-residence certificate or CRS self-certification equivalent
PIF e-invoice XML and issuance log retained for 5 years
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI cross-checks zero-rated invoices against SFEP data and SIGA customs exit records; failure to prove export triggers ITBMS at 7% plus monthly interest (1% per month) and surcharges of 50%-100% of the evaded tax, with possible closure or suspension of the Aviso de Operación. Fraudulent export zero-rating or forged documentation falls within the criminal tax-fraud regime of Ley 70 de 2019 (imprisonment 2-5 years and fines for evasion exceeding B/.100,000), retrospective reassessments for up to 5 years (longer for fraud), revocation of e-invoicing authorization and removal from exporter registries. No statutory FX repatriation deadline applies in Panama's dollarized, exchange-control-free regime; the 180-day window is the internal substantiation benchmark requiring export proceeds to appear in the PIF's bank statements (Stripe/Mercury ACH) within that period to preserve the zero-rating evidence chain.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no issuing central bank; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) acts as banking regulator and prudential authority, Banco Nacional de Panamá performs fiscal agency functions, and the US Dollar is legal tender alongside the pegged Balboa unit (1:1).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully convertible dollarized regime. The Balboa is a token currency at fixed parity with the USD; no exchange controls apply to current account or capital account transactions; profit remittances, dividend distributions, interest payments, and foundation benefit transfers face no prior approval, repatriation, or reinvestment requirements. Withholding taxes attach only to Panama-source income under the territorial tax model.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender regime exists. Export receipts, foreign SaaS revenue, and software subscription collections may be retained indefinitely in USD or other convertible currencies, with no statutorily mandated repatriation timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or documentation filing beyond ordinary banking KYC references.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with clear legal boundaries. Panama has no standalone electronic money institution (EMI) licensing category; any local deposit-taking or financial intermediation requires SBP authorization. An offshore digital EMI is therefore not permitted to solicit deposits or hold Panamanian client funds locally, but a Panama-domiciled PIF may lawfully use US-chartered neobanks (e.g., Mercury for ACH) and global payment aggregators (e.g., Stripe Billing) as collection and settlement rails, subject to each provider's internal country-risk policy, US tax identification requirements, and enhanced UBO disclosure. Crypto-centric EMIs are operationally disfavored under SBP's risk guidance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid model. Beneficial owners and managing directors are not statutorily compelled to appear in person at all institutions; most SBP-licensed banks accept a foundation's resident agent or registered director as the local KYC interviewee and permit a remote video interview for signatories, provided corporate instruments are apostilled and a current beneficiary certificate is issued. A minority of tier-1 banks still insist on at least one physical attendance by the beneficial owner or appointed officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of the Private Interest Foundation structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and registered foundation charter (acta constitutiva), apostilled passports of settlor, directors, and beneficiaries; current certificate of beneficiaries and protector; sworn source-of-funds declaration; six-month personal bank statements for each economic owner; and a formal Panamanian counsel legal opinion tracing the foundation's beneficial ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border cloud infrastructure operations without local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office certificate from the resident agent, resident agent services agreement, board resolutions approving treasury and FX mandates, executed cloud vendor contracts (API/database/DevOps hosting), customer invoicing records, contractor agreements demonstrating engineering administration, and a narrative business plan validating the regional hub role.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits on non-exhaustive name matching
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UN consolidated-screening certificates from a reputable online AML tool, negative PEP results for all officers and beneficiaries, nationality and country-of-residence matrix, corporate group chart, and an SBP-aware compliance counsel letter affirming that any list hit is a confirmed false positive.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency Stripe billing and Mercury ACH settlement volatility resembling structured or clean-shift transaction patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month revenue ledger with per-invoice matching, exporter's management-prepared accounts, Stripe and Mercury reconciliation reports, merchant agreements with processing thresholds, chargeback and refund logs, and proof of exclusive direct ownership of all bank accounts without nominee interference.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections arrive by SWIFT MT103 in USD through US correspondent clearing (Fedwire or CHIPS) using remittance information in field 70 that cites the foundation's charter article and a stated purpose of in-kind capital contribution; Panama imposes no exchange-control or prior-authorization approval, but the receiving SBP-licensed bank conducts corroborative validation of the wire origin, matching legal name, and consistency with the current beneficiary certificate before crediting funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for disbursements are SWIFT MT103 for ordinary vendor payments; commercial letters of credit (L/C) for high-value hardware, procurement, or licensor deposits; and US ACH via a neobank treasury account (Mercury) for recurring cloud subscriptions and developer tooling invoices. Onshore Panamanian USD clearing, through the Automated Clearing House operated by the SBP, is available but reserved for local utility, payroll, or expense disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR FX Forwards (OTC, tenors up to 12 months)
USD/COP and USD/MXN Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) executed with licensed international banks
USD/EUR Cross-Currency Swaps for asset-liability matching on multi-year vendor contracts
European-style FX options on USD/EUR for downside protection on international API and infrastructure procurement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Tax (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus monthly interest of 1%; failure to pay for two consecutive years may lead to a declaration of deactivation and eventual administrative strike-off by the Registro Público after a published notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. Private Interest Foundations are not subject to a compulsory statutory audit. An audit is required only if the Foundation Charter expressly mandates an independent auditor or if the foundation engages in commercial activities that generate Panamanian-source income, triggering general corporate record-keeping rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (Panamanian GAAP) for internal accounting records; no financial statements are required to be filed with the Public Registry or tax authorities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing is required for the Foundation itself. However, the Resident Agent must maintain a current, accurate record of the ultimate beneficial owner(s) at the registered office. Under Panama Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 137 of 2022, any change in the foundation council, founder, executor, or beneficial interest must be reported to the Public Registry and the DGI within 30 calendar days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro de Miembros del Consejo de Fundación)
Resolution / Minutes Book (Libro de Actas y Resoluciones)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by law. If voluntarily commissioned, certified audit fee typically USD 1,000 - USD 2,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation regime: foreign-source income, including dividends, interest, royalties, and capital gains derived outside Panama, is not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) established under Law 25 of 1995 that does not carry on commercial activity within Panama is generally outside the coding of Panama-source business profits and pays only the annual PIF flat government fee of USD 300 through its registered agent. Any Panama-source income, if generated, is taxable at 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 711 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas), filed electronically through Panama's DGI/ATY T@x e-filing portal. A PIF with no Panama-source income generally files a nil return only when required by the DGI and separately settles the annual USD 300 foundation annuity through the registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for the income tax period. Taxpayers with positive Panama-source taxable income may also be subject to quarterly advance corporate income tax payments; a passive Foundation with nil Panama-source taxable income is not required to make such advances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed no later than 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end where the fiscal year corresponds to the calendar year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, filing is due within three months after the close of that fiscal year. The annual PIF annuity fee must be paid by the date determined by the Public Registry, normally during the first quarter of the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (RUC/RED) of the Private Interest Foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Foundation's Panama RUC/RED issued upon registration. If the PIF is treated as non-resident for treaty purposes, the Panama identification remains the filing identifier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year commencement date and closing date of the taxable period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact dates per the PIF's constitutional act and internal accounting records; calendar year is standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aviso de Operación / commercial license number, if any commercial activity is declared in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave blank or enter 'Not applicable' for a passive holding PIF with no Panama commercial license.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Panama-source gross revenue, including Panama-source sales, services, fees, and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 unless the Foundation conducts a business, holds Panamanian real estate, or earns a receivable from a Panamanian obligor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable foreign-source income earned outside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include foreign-source income in taxable Panama-source revenue. Attach an internal schedule showing source country, gross amount, and evidence that management control did not create Panama tax fiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and charges directly attributable to the production of Panama-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 where no Panama-source revenue exists. Foreign administration fees, foreign bank charges, and legal costs are not currently deductible against a zero Panama-source base.
For an offshore PIF, enter 0.00; do not offset foreign losses or expenses against zero Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax determined by applying the 25% rate to net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 where net taxable income is nil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: advance corporate income tax payments, withholding tax credits, and authorized tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 unless the Foundation had Panama-source income and made advance payments or a Panamanian counterparty withheld tax on its behalf.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund claimed for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF with only foreign-source income and no Panama-source activity, enter 0.00. If a refund is claimed on account of withholding, attach official withholding certificates and the bank wire evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger a formal penalty of up to PAB 10,000, a surcharge of 1.5% per month or fraction thereof on any unpaid tax, and statutory interest on the underpayment. Failure to file a perjured or materially incomplete return can attract a penalty of up to 100%–500% of tax evaded. Failure to pay the annual foundation annuity results in registry sanctions, suspension of certificate of good standing, and possible cancellation of the PIF by the registered agent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final withholding on dividends distributed from Panama-source taxable profits of a Panamanian resi dent paying entity. Dividends paid wholly out of foreign-source or already-taxed Panama-source profits are not within the Panama dividend withholding tax under the territorial regime; a PIF beneficiaries' distribution from foreign-source reserves is exempt.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited DTA network. To obtain a reduced DTA withholding rate, the beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a current certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the treaty-resident tax authority; (ii) provide a beneficial ownership declaration and, where relevant, a pension-fund or governmental-entity declaration; (iii) deliver the documents to the Panamanian payer before payment; and (iv) the payer submits the request through the DGI / national tax administration for confirmation. Documents must be retained for at least six years. If the treaty claim is not substantiated before payment, the statutory domestic rate applies and a refund procedure is required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Panama final withholding on Panama-source royalties and interest paid to non-residents is generally 12.5%. Treaty rates, where a DTA applies, can reduce interest to commonly 5%–10% and royalties to 10%–15%, subject to TRC, anti-abuse, and beneficial ownership conditions. Royalties or interest received by a PIF from foreign obligors are foreign-source and fall outside Panama withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 2,500,000 (USD, at parity) of annual Panama-source gross income generally triggers full transfer pricing documentation and reporting obligations; a Local File and Master File are required if annual related-party transactions exceed PAB 250,000 with any single related party. A lower formal reporting threshold may apply to intra-group services and financing arrangements where the PIF acts as a principal.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has not adopted a full OECD-style Economic Substance Regulation applicable to all Private Interest Foundations. Nevertheless, the DGI and AML authorities apply substance-over-form principles: a PIF must maintain board minutes, a fixed or identifiable seat, registered agent records, updated beneficial ownership registers, and a real economic rationale for holding assets and receiving income. A PIF that is a party to cross-border related-party transactions must apply the arm's length principle and maintain contemporaneous evidence. Pure letter-box structures are treated as shell vehicles and may be disregarded for tax, treaty, and AML purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inaccurate characterization of Panama-source income as foreign-source income, omission of Panama-source revenue, fabrication of foreign bank evidence, or submission of a perjured Formulario 711.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of between 100% and 500% of the evaded tax, statutory interest, surcharge of 1.5% per month, and criminal imprisonment for tax fraud under Panama's Penal Code and Fiscal Code. Additionally, the DGI may nullify the return and reassess with presumptive methods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Foundation Council members, registered agent, and signatories can be jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax where the veil is pierced; Panamanian courts may issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, and impose imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Foundation Form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a PIF with no bank account, no books, no board meetings, and no identifiable beneficial owners as a conduit to conceal ownership of developer-tools subscription revenue or API infrastructure contracts from the real economic jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Foundation may be struck off the Public Registry, its assets may be provisionally seized, DTA benefits are denied, and transactions may be recharacterized as direct earnings of the beneficial owner; administrative fines of up to USD 1,000,000 may apply under anti-money-laundering legislation if the conduct is linked to concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may disregard the Foundation and hold the founder, council members, and ultimate beneficial owners personally liable; the registered agent may be sanctioned and barred; travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition procedures are available for foundations used for organized fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party agreements allocating developer infrastructure, data hosting, licensing, or API-monitoring income to the PIF at non-arm's length prices, or paying excessive royalties/technical fees to the Foundation to strip profits from the operating jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A transfer pricing adjustment with statutory interest, an administrative penalty of up to 40% of the adjustment, and a formal fine for the failure to keep contemporaneous documentation; the tax return may be amended retroactively if the DGI identifies a sham transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and finance officers who sign inaccurate cost-pricing declarations may be personally liable for the additional tax and penalties; professional disqualification, travel restriction, and civil claims by creditors may follow where distributions were made to beneficiaries while tax remained unpaid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership information with the UAF or Public Registry, refusal to disclose the real beneficiary of funding routed through an ISIC 6201 developer-tools entity, or using bearer-style foundation powers without a registered beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Panama Law 23 of 2015 and supplementary AML decrees, which may reach USD 1,000,000 per violation; the Foundation's licence and registration may be revoked, and proceeds linked to money laundering are confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, registered agents, and compliance officers may be prosecuted as principals or accomplices; penalties include imprisonment of up to six years for money laundering, travel bans, corporate veil piercing, civil restitution to plaintiffs, and extraterritorial cooperation through INTERPOL.
